A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DistMLIP and contain readable main text, algorithms, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite relocation, renumbering and added appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference timing, simulation capacity, scaling, density sensitivity and distributed-versus-single-device prediction results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds partition-strategy comparisons, expanded timing profiles, a molecular-dynamics stability trajectory and a training benchmark.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain vertical-wall partitioning, border-feature exchange and bond-graph construction for the same four MLIPs. The training demonstration and expanded API explanation do not document a changed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: The original material and biomolecular inference benchmarks remain. Appendix L adds a Li-ion cathode MD stability case, while Appendix M introduces training on the 8.1k-atom GPCR protein 6P9X using Lennard-Jones energy and force labels. This extends evaluated tasks beyond inference benchmarking.

E2.justification: v1 briefly reports qualitative RCM/METIS overhead observations; v2 adds explicit METIS and RCMK comparator rows across five material and biomolecular systems using MACE-3.8M in Appendix K.1. Existing SevenNet and LAMMPS comparisons remain. Despite its caption, the new Table 3 contains no LAMMPS row; those results remain in Table 1.

E3.justification: New protocols include timing-stage profiles across 1, 2, 4 and 8 GPUs under fixed-total and fixed-per-GPU atom counts, and partition-rule substitution while retaining other DistMLIP components. Appendices L–M introduce 2 ns MD with 100k atoms and batch-16 training with 0.4M-parameter CHGNet on eight A100 GPUs. Existing main benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E replaces the limited timing breakdown with scaling-dependent component profiles, including communication and eSEN. Appendix K.1 tests the partitioning-strategy choice, and Appendix L adds long-duration numerical-stability evidence. Existing interaction-range, model-size, density and prediction-alignment analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average the final 10 of 20 scaling-timing trials and use 10 measured trials after five warmups for SevenNet comparisons. v2 introduces no new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports, for example, 101.67 and 98.02 microseconds per atom-step for METIS and RCMK versus 18.20 for vertical walls on 96k water atoms with four GPUs. v2 also adds timing fractions, the 2 ns energy trajectory and 2.1 seconds per training step. v1's absolute timing-breakdown entries are removed; Table 1 and the original plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph-partition, border-node and border-edge definitions and algorithmic mathematics are retained. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation or revised formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit abstract claim of 3.4 times larger systems and up to eightfold faster inference, and highlights the partition-strategy speed comparison in the introduction. It removes the highlighted stress-calculation/isobaric-MD contribution. The central graph-parallel inference-platform contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the new trajectory's initial energy decrease to physical equilibration, explains the partitioning heuristic's advantage over graph traversal, and qualifies large-system training applicability through the difficulty of obtaining quantum-mechanical labels. These add interpretations and applicability boundaries without replacing the original explanations.

D1.justification: Appendix J expands documentation of the Distributed object's inputs and operations, and Appendix M supplies label-generation, batch-size, model-size and hardware details for the training example. Conversely, v2 removes the explicit open-source statement and DistMLIP repository URL. Existing checkpoint links and usage examples remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sriram et al. (2022) and distinguishes graph-parallel training from large-system inference. It also adds Berman, Fatahalian and Duo Zhang references and removes Jones (1924). Existing positioning against spatial partitioning and SevenNet largely remains; publication updates to retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v2 shortens background passages, standardizes foundation-potential terminology, revises the real-world-results discussion, and moves graph-partitioning background and usage examples into appendices. Author contact and conference-header text change, but most prose and the main narrative structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The appendix timing table is replaced by two four-panel stacked-bar figures, while a partition-strategy table and an energy-trajectory figure are added. Existing figures are retained and partly renumbered or relocated; Table 1 and code examples also move. The principal visual change is the substantial expansion and redesign of appendix evidence.

improvement.justification: The partition-strategy comparison, expanded timing profiles and actual 2 ns trajectory strengthen support for efficiency and practical MD use beyond v1's timing and single-step agreement checks. These are useful but bounded gains: the trajectory settings remain sparse, some partition comparisons use unequal atom counts, and the repository pointer is removed. The unchanged core method and original results, together with these reporting limitations, support a limited net improvement.
